chunks: And Yahya ibn Abi 'Imran narrated from Yunus from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The paternal grandfather and the paternal grandmother, and the maternal grandfather and the maternal grandmother, they all inherit.
ai.seo_question: Do paternal and maternal grandparents all inherit in Shia law?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the general rule of inheritance for the four grandparents, establishing that paternal and maternal lines are treated equally in this specific context. While later jurists like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi discuss nuances regarding the 'Hajb' (exclusion) of grandparents by parents or siblings, this hadith serves as the foundational evidence for their right to inherit when not excluded. It highlights the Shia emphasis on equitable distribution across both paternal and maternal kinship branches.
